newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland asks Abidjan for extradition of two sailors.
newsitem.headline: Poland asks Abidjan for extradition of two sailors.

text.p: Poland has applied to Ivory Coast for the extradition of two Polish seamen detained there on suspicion of murdering two German ship officers off West Africa in December, the justice ministry said on Wednesday.
"We are counting on rapid extradition," PAP news agency quoted ministry spokeswoman Barbara Makosa-Stepkowska as saying.

Germany had earlier requested the Poles be extradited to Bonn for trial because the victims and the vessel MV Jannah were German. But Makosa-Stepkowska said Germany had given way and, if extradited, the two would be tried in Warsaw.
She told PAP that although Poland and Ivory Coast did not have an extradition treaty, Poland was applying for the sailors to be handed over under international law.

The ship's crew told police in Ivory Coast that Captain Claus-Herman Clausen and engineer Ulrich Birkelbach, both 50, were stabbed and their bodies tossed overboard as the ship sailed to Abidjan from Port Harcourt, Nigeria, on December 10.
The 11 other crew members handed over the accused to Ivorian police.
Port officials said the 4,455 gross tonne Jannah left Abidjan in December for Hamburg after the two sailors' arrest.
